Deep learning models for knowledge tracing have been lacking in rigorous evaluation, making it nearly impossible to compare new techniques on an universal standard and assess their real-world applicability. To tackle this issue, our team developed a large dataset, called 2M-KT, featuring intricate, realistic learner interaction patterns on a knowledge space, and subsequently established a comprehensive benchmark for developing and evaluating knowledge tracing technologies. We believe 2M-KT will serve as a crucial reference point for future research in this field. Unfortunately, many leading models in the field, including those based on Transformer and RNN architectures, are too computationally intensive to train on our dataset. As such, we conducted a careful evaluation of more efficient models, discovering that they do not consistently excel on 2M-KT, and offering insights into potential areas for enhancing current knowledge tracing technologies.

Given a metric space $(X,d)$, we examine the surjectivity of second-order elliptic operators $u \mapsto -\Delta u + vu$ within the measure class, where $v$ is a non-negative function on $X$. For uniformity conditions satisfied by the underlying space, we determine the set of functions for which these operators are invertible. In addition, we investigate the properties of operators on more complex fractal structures.

Since its presentation at the PxTP workshop in 2014, the veriT format has undergone significant evolution with multiple new features being incorporated. This document serves as a guide to using veriT's advanced capabilities, focusing on notable additions such as recursive procedures, first-order matching, and the ability to define new data types. We have also summarized the proof-checker's capabilities to assist users.

We present a scalable approach for decentralized learning in large networks,
where direct device-to-device communication is limited. To address this limitation,
we introduce FedBuff, an algorithm that combines a centralized server with
local storage on devices. In this setup, data remains localized,
and all communications are either between the server and the devices or among the
devices themselves. As a result of our method's versatility,
the privacy properties and anti-spreading characteristics are preserved,
and when applied to a large network, FedBuff offers improved scalability
while maintaining these benefits. theoretically and empirically,
and specifically, we demonstrate its effectiveness in training deep neural
networks.

This work evaluates whether transfer learning can enhance speech recognition in low-resource languages, specifically Libyan Arabic, by using a library of pre-trained neural networks. The study compares two groups of languages that are either highly or less similar to Libyan Arabic, both within the context of Semitic languages. Assessment metrics include C-Semantic Error and C-Phoneme Error. The results reveal that using prior knowledge from highly similar languages benefits recognition, whereas it may not always be effective for more dissimilar languages. However, when analyzing individual languages, certain less similar languages exhibit a transfer learning benefit, while others show no such improvement, or even a decline in performance. The study's findings are discussed, along with potential explanations and implications, along with proposed directions for future research.

Subsurface navigation tasks often involve uncertain and changing environmental conditions that can be unpredictable, making it a challenging setting for learning-based control systems. Under these complex scenarios, traditional Markov processes may fall short in accurately assessing the current state of a system. To overcome this difficulty, we developed the SPGP-SARSA method, an advanced variation of the SARSA efficiency-enhancing algorithm that integrates GPs for predicting state transitions and uses SPG techniques for more accurate and efficient value estimation. By leveraging the predictive capabilities of GPs and enhancing sampling efficiency through value prediction, SPGP-SARSA allocates more sampling resources to uncertain states while reducing evaluation times. As a more efficient alternative to the existing SPGP-SARSA2 algorithm, our algorithm strategically uses multiple simulations to improve both policy evaluation and optimization. The effectiveness of our approach has been validated through simulated scenarios that are designed to mirror the uncertainties and dynamics of a real underwater vehicle, demonstrating significant enhancements over the traditional SARSA2 algorithm in terms of learning speed and accuracy.

The approach to finding solutions for a relativistic stellar model involving two fluid components can be achieved by utilizing two commuting Killing vectors and modifying the equation of state for each fluid, based on solutions for a single-fluid component. As a demonstration of this method, a known single-fluid solution was adapted by introducing two fluid components and adjusting the respective equations of state, ultimately yielding an exact solution for a rotating neutron star with an elliptical figure.

The effectiveness of language adaptation is crucial and limited errors can have significant consequences. In practical scenarios, it's often necessary to quickly adapt models to new domains or tasks with scarce labeled data. We investigate the challenge of general language error correction adaptation and propose a few-shot transfer learning method called MTCO. Our approach simultaneously addresses the scarcity of correction data and the variability of correction tasks by employing a multi-task contrastive contrastive framework. We enhance the contrastive contrastive framework by incorporating a contrastive contrastive loss function based on corrected documents, resulting in improved performance. Evaluations on multiple datasets show that our method outperforms state-of-the-art GEC adaptation techniques and demonstrates substantial gains over the base model.

We introduce two innovative approaches to enhance existing constant-time mechanisms for divisible cake cutting, focusing on improving fairness for agents with arbitrary valuation functions. Our first method takes any constant-time mechanism and develops a new one where the round-robin version offers improved fairness without increasing computation time. For instance, applying this technique to the cut-and-choose algorithm results in a (1/k)-approximate fair mechanism through round-robin execution. Similarly, our approach can be applied to the even-split method. Our second strategy, targeting the cut-and-choose mechanism, involves an alignment of cuts made by agents, followed by choosing pieces, which yields an allocation that maintains the properties of the original mechanism while ensuring no agent loses out compared to the initial implementation. Our proposed mechanisms are efficient, requiring only two rounds and minimal communication, assuming the number of rounds in the original mechanism is constant.

A comprehensive spectral analysis of UGC 8839, a vibrant spiral galaxy, was conducted using a 4-meter class telescope's high-resolution spectra. The analysis focused on the galaxy's HII region population in the light spectrum, with an emphasis on its outer areas. The studied galaxy was found to have a significant amount of oxygen at a level comparable to the Milky Way, with similar levels found in other spiral galaxies. The rate of ionized oxygen was observed to decrease with increasing distance from the galaxy's center, likely influenced by its low rotational speed in its outer areas. The galaxy's star formation characteristics were also noted to be more active in its outer areas when compared to other similar galaxies.

This study uses Lattice QCD simulations to explore the impact of quark mass changes on the polarizabilities of u/d lattice QCD quarks, with a focus on the relationship between these factors and pion properties. By applying the chiral effective field theory, researchers examined the connection between mass variations and polarizabilities in the mass range of 0.002$\\GeV^2/c^4$ to 0.147$\\GeV/c^2$. The study also incorporated a discussion on the influence of low-lying hadronic states, particularly the $N(1/2^+)$ and $N(3/2^+)$ states, on the results. The data was analyzed in the form of the ratio of the mass variation to the squared mass difference between the $\Delta$ and proton states. The quark mass values were derived from the corresponding pion masses within the L. The calculations were performed on an as.

We analyzed recent extensive observations of CTTS SS Andromedae to gain a deeper comprehension of extreme variability in classical T Tauri stars and how it impacts our ability to interpret variability in accretion rates effectively.  Our study reveals remarkable variability in SS Andromedae's characteristics on different timescales: significant fluctuations in optical and infrared variability are linked to extreme variability in accretion rates, while radio and X-ray variability occur on longer timescales.  The disc's reflectivity and thermal emission in the infrared spectrum show a delay in responding to variability in accretion rates compared to direct thermal emission from accretion shocks.  Our findings also reveal long-term variability in radio and X-ray emissions that outlasts the hydrodynamic timescale of the system.  To better interpret this extended variability, we need a more comprehensive model that considers interactions between the star and the disc.  Our analysis of SS Andromedae's variability on various timescales has been used to assess more simplistic models of accretion and suggests that the variability in radio and X-ray emissions may be associated with global disk instabilities.  Our findings emphasize the importance of extensive variability observations of individual CTTS in advancing our understanding of disk evolution in classical T Tauri stars.

SIT, also known as Shared Individual Trajectories, is an innovative offline multi-agent training method that avoids the need for interaction and imitation learning. In this approach, each agent is asked to analyze and break down the offline training data into a set of segments, with each segment linked to a unique identifier and a corresponding action-value map. Across the entire dataset, these segments and their associated values are shared, allowing the training process to be divided into two distinct offline stages. With these features, SIT exhibits robust generalization capabilities, offering a versatile framework applicable to various domains, from enhancing current methods to addressing entirely new challenges. A simulated environment was used to demonstrate the effectiveness and versatility of SIT, highlighting the significant improvements it achieved over the current state-of-the-art.

This paper introduces a novel Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) based method for medical image registration that combines the capabilities of deep feature extraction using U-Nets and traditional gradient-descent optimization algorithms. Our approach employs two interconnected U-Nets to generate and compare feature maps from source and target images, resulting in a set of image warping parameters that minimize the difference between images. Experimental results show significant improvements over a conventional intensity-based CNN image registration method in both two-dimensional and three-dimensional datasets with added distortions, with lower root-mean-square errors achieved with the proposed CNN based intensity-based image registration approach. Additionally, our results suggest that using CNNs to analyze complex medical images can lead to more efficient and effective results by taking advantage of both feature extraction and intensity-based differences.

Quantum mechanics can be seen as a theory describing single entities through actions they take in responses to hypothetical questions, rather than about nonintuitive collective behaviors among multiple entities. This new single-entity perspective reinterprets nonlocal effects and steering within a local context. We demonstrate that steering and noncontextual effects arise intrinsically within a single-particle system, thereby indicating that their extrinsic, nonlocal manifestations aren't uniquely distinguishing these phenomena. Based on this approach, we utilized interferometers to create distinct states of a single photon via local actions, subsequently verifying these localized states via noncontextual measurements at another location via a beam splitter arrangement. This experiment validates the inherent noncontextual and unlocalizable nature of these quantum states. A key feature of our experiment lies in its ability to establish noncontextual outcomes at one location via uniquely unlocalizable states formed via contextual interference patterns.

The integration of Blockchain technology into IoT Vehicles (IoVs) systems has gained significant attention recently, fueled by the promise of enhanced data security and privacy. While improvements in security and privacy are notable, implementing a blockchain-based solution comes with performance limitations and heightened data protection concerns. This paper delves into these challenges, categorizing them based on performance, partial visibility of blockchain transactions to IoVs devices, the inability to revoke authorized access, and the limited feasibility of implementing smart contracts. A thorough analysis of the limitations of current research is also provided. To address these issues and move forward, this paper outlines several performance optimization strategies, suggests ways to mitigate performance drawbacks, discusses the possibility of access revocation, and provides a roadmap for effective smart contract design. By identifying key performance bottlenecks and offering potential solutions, this paper serves as a foundation for developing more efficient, secure, and private blockchain-based solutions for IoVs applications.

Following its nova eruption, V392 Per's accretion system required nearly a year to regain the mass eruption rate it had previously possessed. Based on observations from V392 Per's early recovery phase using data from the All-Sky Automated Survey and the 1.8-meter and 3.6-meter telescopes at Kitt Peak National Observatory, our analysis of the system's light curves and spectral properties led to the following key findings: following its eruption, V392 Per's spectrum exhibited significant enhancement in the emission lines of hydrogen and helium, along with an estimated mass eruption rate of 1x10^-7 solar masses per year. Furthermore, our analysis of the system's optical and UV spectral energy distributions revealed that a black body with a temperature of approximately 16,000 Kelvin was responsible for the majority of the systems' radiation. Additionally, our study of V392 Per's recovery phase using data from the 3.6-meter telescope revealed that the system's behavior could be explained by an model in which the mass eruption rate was restricted by the accretion disc's ability to break through during the nova outburst.

The feedback encoding scheme in current FDD systems requires a lot of resources due to long code words and extensive pilot transmissions. In an attempt to improve efficiency, this paper explores two key areas: reducing the size of feedback codes and minimizing pilot resources. A novel approach is proposed that utilizes training symbols already present in uplink data to carry downlink information, eliminating the need for additional overhead. Furthermore, a precoder-based scheme is developed to optimize performance without relying on extensive code words. In contrast, the Lloyd clustering methods commonly used result in suboptimal outcomes with increased resource consumption. Both of our proposed methods are designed to operate with existing overheads and demonstrate through simulations that they provide significant gains over traditional methods.

We present new results on surface currents arising at the interface of two half-spaces with varying bulk anomaly robustness. At this interface, tripartite surface currents arise and defy conventional expectations by defying their typical right-handed orientation; they instead exhibit a left-handed direction. These surface currents maintain their stability under multiple conditions and calculations verify their accuracy using past findings as well as a tripartite Mello-Shamoon equation. We further derive a general relationship between the surface currents and the anomaly robustity gap using this tripartite Mello-Shamoon equation.

In 1961, Brans and Dicke modified general relativity theory by introducing a non-minimal coupling of a scalar field to the metric tensor. Subsequently, Landau analyzed the behavior of Brans-Dicke theory during a binary neutron star merger. Based on Landau's work, we investigated the circumstances under which Brans-Dicke theory could match the observation that most observed gravitational waves have no indication of a scalar field component. By examining the binary neutron star merger using state-equation-dependent numerical relativity simulations, we found that the far-field Brans-Dicke solution can be obtained by simulation data. In particular, whether the binary star merger results in the emission of a scalar wave that cannot escape to null infinity or instead discharges to infinity depends on the equation of state. It is also influenced by the Brans-Dicke coupling parameter, $\omega_{\rm BD}$. For instance, when the dimensionless Brans-Dicke parameter exceeds 1400, RPT-E quark star mergers can give rise to a magnetar that steadily emits a scalar wave component to infinity. In addition, we mapped Brans-Dicke parameter spaces for RPT-E quark star mergers.

We investigated the characteristics of the density of merger rates for Population III
binary black holes by utilizing a merger rate for single Population III black holes,
combined with gravitational wave observations from LIGO-Virgo and theoretical calculations.
The results indicate that the density of merger rates for Population III binary black holes
reaches a peak at a redshift of approximately 15, with an estimated peak rate of between
$10^{-9}$ and $10^{-7}$ per year per cubic Mpc. This range falls within the uncertainty
margins of direct constraints from the Planck satellite, suggesting that the peak may be
supported by an early formation of Population III black binaries. However, if the merger
rate for single Population III black holes is on the lower end of the estimated range, the
peak density of Population III binary black hole mergers occurs before a redshift of 10,
leading to a predicted separation between their merger signals and gravitational waves from
primordial inflation.

This study focuses on secure beamforming techniques for risk mitigation in wireless systems. Initially, we investigate two methods of resource allocation to ensure risk-based communication security. The first method of allocation impacts system security but offers operational simplicity, whereas the second method affects both security and privacy aspects. Our analysis reveals the impact of information asymmetry on beamforming strategies and provides insights into adequate security levels achievable via power allocation. Furthermore, we examine the effects of various information scenarios on both communication performance and security. A risk-sensitive utility function is employed to identify an optimal level of information transparency. Additionally, we introduce an end-to-end utility that integrates technical performance, data privacy, and policy-driven risk management goals. This utility function allows for the identification of robust and efficient power allocation strategies, even in conditions of limited information.

Recent advancements in computing power and large-scale text data have fueled the growth of digital text-based games. Consequently, the simulation of complex, real-world scenarios through text game scripts has been proposed and analyzed. However, advancing this field requires a significant investment in computing resources due to the slow processing speed of text-based games. To address this limitation, we have developed a high-throughput text game simulation platform called TextWorldExpress. By leveraging full-text GPU acceleration and a customized engine optimized for specific game scripts, we have achieved a 300x increase in simulation throughput compared to using traditional text parsing methods. In addition, our platform's flexibility allows for the seamless integration of various game modifications, demonstrating a utility that has been validated through the successful replication of prior research and applications of the TextAI challenge.

In recent years, deep learning has seen a significant growth, driving the need for highly efficient hardware designs. Current research has explored various optimized models, including tensor factorization based approaches. Although these designs offer substantial improvements in speed and energy efficiency, they fall short in flexibility due to their fixed functionality. To bridge this gap, we present a dynamic reconfigurable hardware architecture called FDHT-LSTM, which integrates variable fuzzy logic, LSTM, and attention modules and can adapt to specific requirements by dynamically changing its components. This architecture, FDHT-LSTM features a lookup based fuzzy logic controller, a fully unrolled LSTM, an attention module that efficiently processes data, and a dataflow design that efficiently manages memory. We implemented this design in 28nm CMOS, and it can speedily process five different models, a feat no other dedicated hardware designs can achieve. In terms of performance, FDHT-LSTM outperforms similar dedicated designs by a factor of 1.7 in terms of throughput and 2.8 in terms of energy efficiency, while also featuring 10 bits of precision and a maximum operating frequency of 500MHz.

In spaces with negative curvature, also known as anti-de Sitter (adS) spaces, the principles of the Weak Gravity Conjecture present significant challenges due to the complex behavior of signals in these spaces. This paper proposes a novel interpretation of WGC self-binding energy, independently calculated for both particles and fields within the AdS context. Determining self-binding energy requires a threshold for when trapped signals can no longer escape, which is unfeasible in AdS spaces beyond a certain size. As a result, self-bound field candidates cannot exist within these spaces, leading to profound implications: either the AdS WGC must prohibit extremely large spaces or the adS vacuum stability cannot coexist with certain field theories.

Let $(A, \mathfrak{n})$ be a Noetherian local ring of characteristic $p > 0$. In this setting, local rings within the zero submodule of $\mathfrak{n}^*[A]$ indicate that $A$ is not F-rational, in contrast, if $A$ is F-rational, it is true for all $A$-modules whose length is finite. In this paper, we demonstrate in a regular local ring $A$, the zero submodule of local cohomology $H^1(\operatorname{Spec} A)$ consists of all quotients $\operatorname{quot}(f)$ parameterized by $\operatorname{fract}(g)$. In this context, both parameterizing and orbiting sets are defined based on the deep equalities operator $\operatorname{F}_a$-skew for analogous operator sets. In addition, we establish a relationship between the zero submodule of local cohomology $H^1(\operatorname{Spec} A)$ and $\operatorname{ann}^*(A)$ in relation to test elements generated by operator sets that are both progressive and lex.

This paper delves into the global dynamics of NEMO, a multi-market model consisting of optional trading opportunities for energy producers in different markets with varying levels of competitiveness. The market model is analyzed mathematically through an all-or-none order design in the highest market segment, leading to a situation where the primary objective of the grid operator to efficiently manage energy demand can result in extensive procurement. The initial findings of this study are illustrative and can be applied to energy policy in grid systems with significant optional energy production capacity. An initial all-or-none trading design in the higher market segment, combined with limited production costs, may lead to inefficient energy management and unnecessary purchases from more expensive energy sources. The phenomenon of NEMO is explored through a detailed examination of the dynamics between the more advantageous O&M market and the less competitive OEM market. The analysis reveals that the grid operator's procurement decisions are influenced by the levels of optional energy production capacity and the variability of energy demand. The NEMO model is formulated mathematically through a rigorous optimization problem, and the market models of VCM and BTM are incorporated to simulate the effects of different trading designs. The simulation results demonstrate the impact of NEMO on grid efficiency and provide policy recommendations to mitigate the risks of NEMO.

Given an algebraically closed field $K$ of a characteristic different from 2 and an integer $n$ that is not a perfect square, there is an absolute upper bound $\Qn{un}$ for the size of Galois groups generated by linear transformations in $GL_2(K[n])$. This result builds upon and relates to earlier works, including a connection to the polynomial version of the Bateman-Horn conjecture, with implications that could potentially support a polynomial hypothesis introduced by J. Ellermeyer. In contrast, when the characteristic is 0 or when it matches the integer $n$, we derive new, previously unknown bounds for these Galois group generators.

Recent observations from the Stratospheric, Tropospheric and Ultraviolet Invisible (SUVUVI) instrument aboard the Saturnian satellite mission (Saturn) revealed unusual warmth and warmth retention near Saturn's north polar stratosphere during the summer season.  These observations stood in stark contrast to the cold North Polar Stratospheric Vortex (NPSV) that characterized the winter and spring months of the previous hemisphere.  As the planet entered the southern polar stratospheric summer months of 2008-2009, researchers discovered that temperatures near the south polar stratosphere were significantly cooler than anticipated, marking the beginning of the formation of a cold vortex.  This study will examine the seasonal variations and atmospheric dynamics affecting the polar stratospheric vortex of the gas giant (Saturn).

In this paper, we investigate the local well-posedness and blow-up properties of solutions to the $L^2$-critical NLS equation in both whole space and a bounded domain, in the presence of an $\alpha$-fractional Nemytskii nonlinearity. We derive an sufficient condition for blow-up in both scenarios, specifically for radial data when the nonlinearity lies within a range related to $\alpha$. We also prove that a certain set of initial conditions will lead to blow-up within a short, predictable time frame. We have further established that a recent, conjectured result by Glassey can be achieved when $\alpha$ is between 1 and 2, in both whole space and a bounded domain, in the presence of an Nemytskii nonlinearity. We have also investigate the effect of the domain's boundary on the critical nature of the blow-up results, showing that the presence of the boundary can lead to a narrower range of $\alpha$ values for which blow-up may occur.

This paper explores methods for analyzing and investigating polynomial
systems over fields with non-zero characteristics using Sage and NumPy. It
begin by outlining the necessary components for polynomial computation in
characteristic-zero fields within Sage and then extends this analysis to
fields of characteristic-p. The discussion includes creating fields of
characteristic-p, both manually and automatically, along with techniques
for polynomial computation in such fields. Examples are provided to
demonstrate polynomial computation in fields of characteristic-p. Additionally,
the text refers to external resources, including a YouTube video, that offer
further information on polynomial computation in fields of characteristic-p
using Sage.

This research extends the symplectic double vector bundle theory to a generalised n-fold version, leveraging the geometric properties of symmetric n-fold vector bundles. By examining the tangent structure of symmetric $n$-fold vector bundles, we established a correspondence with n-fold cotangent bundle structures, a relationship that in the case of the double variant leads to a characterization of symplectic double vector bundles as a natural setting for Manin products. A similar analysis of the super-tangent structure yields a description of the Td-super-double bundle, which constitutes a symmetric double vector bundle and enables the formation of a quadratic super-manin product.

Geometric properties are investigated for the Gelfand-Naimark algebra under the action of a specific Lie algebra group, namely $Sp(4,\mathbb{R})$.  This action is examined using measures developed by V. Kiriillov and T. Stantchev.  The relationship between these two measures is derived and the geometric characteristics of the measure are further explored.  Additionally, the relation between Kiriillov's measure and the geometric measure on certain algebraic orbits is investigated.

This work introduces a novel phase-retrieval method based on gradient descent in the space of energy distributions, aiming to improve the resolution of x-ray scattering data. Energy spectra can no longer be freely adjusted to match the observed scattering patterns, rather, only probability distributions are sought that, when inserted into the x-ray scattering equation, yield an optimal fit to the measured data. A key innovation involves an x^{1/3} probability distribution constraint designed to prevent unphysical solutions and facilitate rapid convergence. By utilizing an x-ray scattering simulator as part of the learning process, we teach a start with an existing energy spectrum. Numerous tests were conducted on synthetic datasets to assess the algorithm's performance, and results showed it could efficiently and accurately recover energy spectra, even from noise-affected x-ray scattering measurements.

This research develops a method to simulate complex fracture patterns in porous materials, where some parts of the medium become completely unfractured, similar to "shadow" areas. A new direction is taken in this work by examining a specific `$\beta$` function from quantum field theory, which is approached from a classical perspective and modified to handle these extreme fracture conditions. Consequently, a corresponding change in pressure is derived from the modified `$\beta$` function and the Dirac operator. The validity of this modeling technique is demonstrated through various test scenarios, including a comparison with a previously established model.

Decision-making processes in real-world scenarios heavily depend on selecting the most suitable hypothesis from various possibilities. Traditionally, this problem has been tackled by assigning a score to each option and choosing the one with the highest value. However, this method's simplicity can lead to suboptimal outcomes. A more effective approach is to use utility functions, which consider multiple factors, including redundancy and diversity, to facilitate nuanced comparisons and rankings. In this paper, we present a comprehensive review of research related to utility functions for support task decision-making, examining how they can be applied to various settings, one of which is unbalanced hypothesis distribution. We explore the challenges associated with this issue and discuss potential solutions, while also highlighting promising directions for future investigation.

Our analysis of the intricate connections between sentences is significantly
enriched by a newly created dataset known as DiscSense, which comprises
nearly 55,000 entries of three-sentence combinations paired with corresponding
discourse functionalities and patterns. This pattern, specifically designed to
support more accurate predictions of inter-sentence relationships, has also
been demonstrated in a notable improvement of 4-to-3-sentence inter-sentence
relationship prediction using a BERT-based model, resulting in a substantial
enhancement of 5.1 points.

This paper introduces fundamental geodesic strong convexity and smoothness properties to a novel factorized objective known as MaxVol, in a specific setting with a partially linear nonconvex loss function and a linear transformation applied to a convex component. Leveraging these geometric characteristics in the setting of linear regression with matrix coefficients, we demonstrate the efficiency of the gradient descent algorithm applied to the MaxVol objective when trained on an isometric data set. Our analysis reveals that with an appropriate learning rate, the algorithm achieves optimal statistical accuracy while maintaining optimal computational complexity. Our findings provide a linear interpretability to a recent state-of-the-art algorithm, MaxVol, which previously exhibited nonconvex behavior even in the simplest setting of linear regression with a single variable.

Pptcbi3eg: In 1990, J.A. Searle conjectured that for bipartite graphs, the strong edge-coloring number for any bipartite graph with a maximum degree of 3 should not exceed 10. In 2009, Dvořák modified this by proposing an upper bound of 12. Pptcbi3eg: This research identifies specific classes of bipartite graphs with a maximum degree of 3 where the strong edge-coloring number is equal to 8 or 9. This includes paths, stars, cycles of even length, and certain configurations formed by combining these elements. Moreover, we develop general principles to analyze more intricate structures. Nevertheless, it is established that if the pptt contains a particular type of configuration consisting of six edges arranged in a particular manner, the strong edge-coloring number is at least 10.

This study applies co-evolutionary algorithms to a rock-paper-scissors game, with the goal of identifying strategies that are difficult to counter. To assess alignment between the evolved strategies and theoretical predictions, we employed genetic algorithms paired with NashEqui fitness evaluation, resulting in evolved strategies that exhibit symmetric expected distances from the Nash Equilibrium, but with unequal treatment of rock, paper, and scissors due to initial program biases. When comparing social and individual learning methods, we found that strategies under the individual learning scenario demonstrate a superior expected distance from the Pareto Front of Nash Equilibria. Furthermore, when testing two variations of the genetic algorithm - one based on replacement and another on mutation - the former produced evolved strategies with a more advantageous distance from the Nash Equilibrium.

Consider a weighted oriented graph, denoted as $O_w(\mathcal{G})$, built upon an underlying undirected graph $ \mathcal{G} $. We establish the equality between the ordinary and symbolic powers for the edge ideal of a weighted oriented tree and its power levels. Additionally, the condition for the equality to hold for any oriented graph is also determined.

This paper presents a novel approach to preventing silent data corruptions in deployed machine learning systems, which provides a unified framework for non-uniform numerical alterations, including inserting false positives and altering data without detection. To tackle this issue, we put forth multiple innovative methods to corruptions prevention, and evaluated our solutions in silent data corruptions' detection. Our results demonstrate that our techniques considerably improve the identification of silent data corruptions, and also reveal common causes of silencing in optimized neural networks, which produce characteristic patterns of insertions and alterations. Furthermore, we observed that silencing effectiveness varies greatly across neural network components and recommend two silencing-preventing techniques, silence estimation and non-uniform quantization optimization, and showed that these methods can significantly enhance corrupted-system detection, and successfully identify several silencing sources that caused bugs in real-world incidents. To disseminate our findings, we contributed data in the SilentText dataset, and contributed code to the PyQuant library.

We have adapted the basic Jordanian twist concept from Lie algebra $so(2,1)$ at a specific value of the parameter $\lambda$ = 1, producing a generalized version applicable for two distinct cases: $\alpha$ < 1 and $\alpha$ > 1, each associated with a distinct set of non-local generators through a change of basis transformation. This generalized twist has led to the formation of the $\Lambda_\alpha$-deformed Lie algebraic structure in finite dimensions. By utilizing this generalized twist in the context of the Lagrangian quantum field theory, we have derived the corresponding quasi-Hopf T-matrix and fuzzy sphere operator. Additionally, the Fubini-Study metric has been calculated before the introduction of the deformed gravitational field theory and the associated $\alpha$-dependent Einstein's equations have been determined.

The challenge of tagging names in languages with limited resources is a crucial task in natural language processing. To address this issue, our proposed method called Aggregated Cross-lingual Pretrained Tagger enhances existing techniques by aggregating multiple translated languages' names and entity labels into a multilingual sequence labeler. Using multilingual named entity recognition datasets from six languages, our experiments demonstrate that our approach significantly boosts the performance on the smaller language sets. Specifically, we observed up to a 1.5-point improvement in F1 score over the baseline on average and our results indicate that our technique is particularly effective for languages with scarce resources.

This research examines various pair combinations including protons, neutrons, deuterons, He3, Li5, Lambda, Sigma0, Xi0, Omega- baryons as well as K+, K-, pi+ mesons in comparison to K*0 and pi0 particles. These comparisons involve both hadronic families and different species within them. Such analyses focus on ratios between particle yields at intermediate transverse momenta ($p_{\perp}$ ranges from 1 to 5 GeV/c). Initial findings reveal consistent patterns across multiple collision types including central Au+Au, Cu+Cu, and p+p+ events at the same $p_{\tau}$ values. Notably, interesting deviations from expected radiative equilibrium conditions have emerged in small-scale collisions involving p+p+, Cu+Cu systems in the same centralities. These patterns may hint at possible phase transition mechanisms leading to quark-gluon plasma formation. A detailed investigation has been carried out through various theoretical models including coalescence, statistical hadronization, and transport approaches in an attempt to explain these observed characteristics.

The impact of a city's infrastructure layout on the patterns of civil disturbances is a new area of study for social scientists.  In this paper, we use a cellular automaton model set in three different city layouts to investigate this phenomenon.  Our model shows that the topological structure of a city can lead to scalable patterns of protest activity, similar to power laws seen in real-world data.  By incorporating spatial interactions into the model, we observe even more complex dynamics, including rapidly changing frequencies of events and cluster formation.  Our findings highlight the importance of understanding the physical layout of a city in modeling and predicting the dynamics of civil unrest.

This article introduces a bracing operator from Brzozowski's operator repertoire to a selective set, forming part of a bracing operator-based symbolic decision process for verifying inclusion when a target is a general regular expression. By utilizing this operator, our method confirms that specific-p types of predicates vanish from a set, ultimately removing them from a bracing operator suite. In addition to its unique features, our decision process incorporates strong conciseness properties and an algorithm that checks the inclusion of a specific-p type of expressions in another set of expressions. Furthermore, our approach encompasses Brzozowski's original approach while also incorporating its bracing operator variants and precomputation optimizations.

This paper provides an in-depth review of vision-inertial odometry (VIO) methods, focusing on the evolving data processing techniques from conventional models to deep learning (DL) solutions. We categorize VIO approaches based on how they handle data processing, analyzing traditional and hybrid models' preprocessing techniques, as well as the diverse methods employed in DL-based pipelines, including spatial and temporal data fusion, and the use of recurrent and convolutional architectures. By presenting the related algorithms in a unifying framework, we offer clear insights into the similarities and differences among the various approaches. Additionally, an extensive discussion on datasets employed in VIO evaluation is included to complement the pipeline analysis. This work is intended to serve researchers in the field of simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM) by facilitating efficient literature searches, streamlining datasets comparisons, and aiding in the development of robust and accurate odometry models across different data processing stages.

We present a theoretical framework for higher-order Weyl semimetals in three dimensions with square-root topology. By breaking symmetries and altering the Hamiltonian from its higher-order Wilson loop gapless Weyl points, we demonstrate two distinct non-linear non-trivial topological non-linear phases. The first non-linear non-trivial topological phase exhibits non-vanishing polarizability Valley Hall effect. The second non-linear non-trivial topological phase exhibits an anomalous Hall effect. Both non-linear non-trivial topological phases exhibit non-trivial Wilson loop and non-linear non-trivial topological characteristics along all three crystallographic directions, setting them apart from conventional higher-order topological non-linear non-trivial properties.

This study provides a numerical analysis of data interpolation on manifolds, focusing on the use of edge finite elements to fill in missing data. We investigate how different patterns of missing data affect the accuracy of our nomenclature models' outputs. Our notes cover a range of grid densities and types, using both one- and two-edge elements, and summarize our key findings in table format.

Knowledge amalgamation in Neural Machine Translation aims to integrate distinct, non-aggressive models into a single, superior model. Creating a representative training corpus, a crucial aspect, involves using a knowledgeable corpus filtered by relevance and a neutral, non-biased translation process employing a salience-based method. Although the approach showed promising results in practice, understanding the underlying principles due to its lack of a performance-driven analysis. This study conducts an in-depth examination of the salience-based translation process by evaluating the generated representations through a combination of quantitative and qualitative means. Additionally, focusing on the efficiency of training the student model, a new loss function is introduced, called Maximum a Posteriori (MAP) loss, yielding significant improvements over the original process. Overall, the study introduces an innovative framework for understanding the representation learning in NMT knowledge amalgamation and achieves better performance by refining the salience-based process.

Given two elliptic curves without complex multiplication within the same genus 0 field, we, denote them $E_1$ and $E_2$, seek to identify all $M$-quart expansions within this specific category where $E_1$ and $_2$ do not increase in rational rank. For each specified rational rank range, we provide a precise formula in terms of this rank for the number of S4 quartic extensions, noting that these ranges include [0,1), [1,5/81), and [5/81, 1). Furthermore, we establish that a generic elliptic curve within this category will not gain rank when combined with $E_1$ and $E_2$.

Quantum quenches in many-body systems trigger time-evolution that can be both computationally and physically demanding to calculate over extended periods. To reduce this demand, previous studies established the correlation between the rate of irreversible entropy production and initial conditions by comparing the irreversible entropy production rate and the total irreversible entropy produced. Our team has developed an algorithm to calculate the reversible and irreversible components of the total produced entropy directly from the time-dependent density matrix. This new method enabled us to calculate the initial correlations between the entropy production rate and the total produced entropy in spin-1/2 Heisenberg model for a range of quenched parameters.

We present an alternative non-unitary dynamics theory arising from an open-system perspective, where the reduced dynamics of the system can be described using a non-unitary evolution operator within a specific time interval, with environment-induced non-unitarity and a non-trivial initial system-environment correlation. Rather than assuming a typical environment-initial state, we time-twirl the total state including the environment, yielding a new effective initial state and deriving environment-induced non-unitary dynamics as a consequence. This approach yields the effective evolution operator as a byproduct, or alternatively the time-twirling yields a statistical average over possible unitary dynamics units. Furthermore, we show that in the short-time regime where the non-unitary dynamics occurs, time-twirling yields the same dynamics units. We also provide a relation between the non-unitary dynamics units and the initial state properties, including the system's distinguishability time. Rather than the density matrix, we describe the initial state properties using a purifier in the environment and show that the effective evolution operator arises from the environment-initial state unitary dynamics units. Finally, we illustrate our theory with concrete examples, including the quantum Jaynes-Cummings model, and verify our results with numerical simulations.

This research paper investigates specific mathematical functions known as Boolean vertices, which are formed by specific combinations of variables and their values. We focus on vertex configurations within an n-dimensional space that can accommodate a nondegenerate regular simplex, a particular geometric shape. By applying Cramer's rule and/canonical form techniques, we are able to characterize spaces capable of containing a regular simplex vertex configuration. Furthermore, we can determine the side lengths of these simplices in spaces capable of containing them. Our findings, however, are limited by the application of these methods and may not represent the complete solution to this problem.

Etched silicon (ES) has been produced via a meticulous four-step etching process applied to high-resistivity silicon, and its etched surfaces have been filled with silicon to a depth of approximately 300 nm. Comparatively, etched silicon with a significantly thicker etched layer (ETSL), at around 10 microns, has been created using standard texturing techniques. Both ES and ETSL samples underwent carrier concentration measurements utilizing the van der Pauw method. Notably, the carrier concentration in ES was observed to be roughly 10 times lower than in ETSL, with an even more substantial difference when considering the substantial thickness discrepancy between ES and ETSL. Potential causes for this high intrinsic carrier concentration have been identified and may have implications for the development of highly efficient photovoltaic technologies.

Interior-exterior cycling within a planet could influence its atmospheric evolution over time.  Venus presents an intriguing case, with evidence of recent surface water and surface and lower atmosphere geological activity, while also showing significant global temperature variations and surface age.  We developed a coupled model involving a one-dimensional atmosphere and a two-step surface energy balance equation to examine the long-term atmospheric and geological history of Venus.  This model accounts for surface heat flow, plate tectonics, magnetic field generation, and plate subduction, and was used to simulate the evolution of Venus for a range of CO2 outgassing and volatile recycling scenarios between 4 billion years ago and the present time.  Our model results, however, require much more complex atmospheric and geological modeling with detailed cloud feedback and extended GCMs, and also indicate that even minor changes in plate tectonics, magnetic field generation, and plate subduction can significantly impact the interpreted timeline of Venus's evolution.

In this work, we formulate and analyze a non-linear multivariate point process model that incorporates various interaction phenomena through the non-linear Hawkes process. We derive expressions for the steady-state intensities and investigate their stability under specific conditions. Furthermore, we establish that these processes can be represented through a non-linear input/output structure. Specific instances, including the quadratic and binary Hawkes processes, are examined in detail. Statistical inference based on historical data is also discussed. The paper concludes with numerical experiments to assess our proposed estimation methods.

A new method is proposed for linear polarized light polarpation using a plasma, a technique potentially suitable for space polarimeters. The necessary thickness for achieving complete polarization is much thinner than existing methods, particularly when used in high electron density plasma and when operating with weak magnetic fields. For example, it could be realized using a few centimeters of a high-temperature plasma in a weak magnetic field. Although the requirement of a high plasma maintenance may pose challenges, it could be accomplished with a localized plasma located between optical systems components. However, Poynting Roberts effect in a stronger magnetic field over a thinner plate may hinder its application for scientific research, although it could be useful for practical devices like satellite instruments.

We conducted an in-depth analysis of the ttH scenario within the standard model, incorporating a second Higgs doublet that could potentially explain the observed CP violation in tau leptons. Our investigation included the complete one-loop electroweak radiative corrections to the Higgs-boson mediated processes contributing to the tau electric dipole moment. By utilizing the full set of massless fermion doublet QED counter-terms, we derived the complete one-loop radiative corrections, which amount to approximately 15% for both cross-sections and the electric dipole form factor in processes involving tau lepton pair production.

This paper investigates the error correction capabilities of rank metric codes in relation to their rates, a property that behaves differently for rates less than 1/2 and rates greater than 1/2. To achieve this analysis, we utilize an transformation known as generalized row reduction, a tool previously employed to construct such codes. For rates less than 1/2, we utilize properties of the generalized reduction matrix, whereas for rates above 1/2, we leverages its use in encoding to identify key characteristics. As a result of our approach, we can establish bounds on the rank metric erasure correction capability achievable by any linear code with a specific rate. Notably, our results improve and simplify previously known rates achieved by efficient encoding algorithms for minimum rank metric erasure correction.

In the context of holographic CFT$_2$, we analyze the behavior of conserved current OPE blocks through a geodesic operator framework in AdS$_2$. By comparing our findings to prior adS$_3$ geodesic operator calculations, we observe that the AdS$_2$ geodesic operators fail to form a self-contained representation of the CFT$_2$ vacuum block. Rather, our results suggest an indispensable need for singular AdS$_2$ geodesic operators to accurately model the vacuum block in CFT$_2$. In the case of large central charge $c$, these additional operators are identified with specific falling modes of the gauge field. In contrast, within the adS$_3$ framework, these corresponding modes are absent due to appropriate boundary conditions. In the AdS$_2$ scenario, we derive the correlation functions of these extra modes by employing the Witten diagram method.

In 1991, Gelfand and MacPherson introduced the concept of the free Lie algebra combinatorial differential manifold to calculate the combinatorial de Rham cohomology of Lie algebras combinatorial manifolds. Building upon this foundation, we developed a new framework: the charged free charged free Lie algebra combinatorial differential manifold and a new type of combinatorial differentiable manifold known as the charged Lie algebra combinatorial differentiable manifold. By utilizing these innovations, we were able to derive a pivotal result proving that the (combinatorial de Rham cohomology for a combinatorial differentiable manifold) is exactly one in the first cohomological group and null in all other positive integer cohomological groups when applied to the free charged free Lie algebra combinatorial differentiable manifold. Furthermore, when examined through the lens of a specific class of differentiable combinatorial structures called stratified sets, the (combinatorial de Rham cohomology for a specific differentiable combinatorial structure) matches precisely with the well-established results obtained using logarithmic forms.

Ni/Fe ratios in core-collapse supernovae are typically higher than in collapsars for a given mass of Ni produced.  SN~2020jfo exhibited a spectrum inconsistent with standard models but could be explained by a shock-heated Ni/Fe profile in a core-collapse event.  In contrast, SN 1987A's spectrum matched theoretical predictions but with lower Ni/Fe ratios.  Two spectra from SN 2020jfo, observed between 4.7 and 9.2 days after explosion and at 3300 km/s, were matched by snippets from synthetic spectra, indicating the presence of multiple velocity layers.  Based on its properties, SN~2020jfo is more like SN 1987A but with a 2-5 times stronger Ni/Fe ratio, which is also reflected in its peak to tail luminosity ratio of 1.1 compared to 2.8 for SN 1987A.  Although SN~2020jfo's Ni/Fe ratio is intriguingly high, it is important to note that its spectrum was influenced by several factors including electron capture, proton and neutron skews, and the absence of certain elements like oxygen, Ti, Mn, Co, Cu, Zr, and Zn found in SN 1987A's ejecta. Loops within a lobster-eye optical system are arranged in rows and columns, with detectors behind them to create cross-shaped images that change with the azimuthal angle of the arrangement's rotation. Analyzing the diagonal bright lines in these cross images can accurately determine the exact location of each row and column, providing an efficient method for identifying and aligning a lobster-eye optical system using only its output. This approach is particularly beneficial in applications where it is challenging to insert or attach an object with a point source image into the target area.

Utilizing a methodology first developed by Daskalopoulos, Gerber and Sideris to examine the Dirichlet problem of the Chern-Lambe equation on the unit ball, we can apply this approach to analyze various nonlinear equations on an arbitrary domain in $\mathbb{R}^n$. Specifically, our primary contribution involves resolving the boundary value problem of the Chern-Lambe equation on the unit ball and the characterization of the unique operator within the Chern-Lambe family. Furthermore, we can address the BVP of the Chern-Lambe equation on a general domain. Moreover, our methodology also applies to other equations, demonstrating its versatility and broad applicability.

We employ an extended $\Lambda$RADON simulation to the "Swamp" dataset, a highly non-Gaussian initial condition, in an effort to determine whether a density-only model can accurately predict halo masses. Our findings reveal that, at the minimum halo mass that can be captured by the simulation, a density-only model is incapable of forecasting halo masses beyond what the radial component of the halo occupancy model can explain. Conversely, within the mass range where dark halo properties are fully Gaussian, our results indicate that models considering only density fail to accurately predict halo masses. This is in contrast to models considering both density and velocity, which closely match the halo mass assembly within a 10% margin. These findings are consistent across two distinct cosmological parameters. To further investigate, we analyze the effects of reducing the non-Gaussianity amplitude and increasing the non-Gaussianity amplitude, as well as the impact of rotational effects in a specific mass range. Our findings have direct implications for the interpretability of the $\Lambda$RADON model, as well as the development of halo mass proxies and dark matter N-body simulations.

The newly introduced 'aniso' module within the Star formation and evolution code enables a more intricate rotating star model by incorporating variable angular momentum and mixing mechanisms. Unlike conventional conservative conservation methods, the 'aniso' module uses an anisotropic fluid model, assigning rotating fluid properties like mass and angular momentum to individual fluid elements based on their angular position rather than preserving these properties through conservative methods. Preliminary one-dimensional rotating star models developed using the 'aniso' module align closely with non-rotating models by Miggaerts, while models with low angular momentum exhibit characteristic rotationally induced features, including increased equatorial overlap and rapid rotation suppression of inner pressure nodes. The models also predict angular momentum redistribution due to the rotation-induced Coriolis force and altered stellar properties, including increased equatorial mass loss, altered moment of inertia, and mass transfer in binary systems.

Training powerful machine learning models relies on acquiring and processing large amounts of high-quality annotated data. Making an informed decision about where to invest limited resources for annotation can be compared to exploring a vast, partially known landscape to discover the most valuable locations for data annotation. In this context, a novel framework called the Convex Label Exploration Problem was developed to map out the complex, non-convex label importance terrain using streamlined, convex operations. This problem focuses on identifying a small set of expensive labels that, when combined with previously obtained information,助力 maximizes the performance of a machine learning model trained on high-quality annotated data. We show how the non-convex label importance terrain can be effectively contained within a manageable, convex framework to guide optimal label selection. A novel iterative approach was proposed to, step by step, outline the most informative regions of the label exploration landscape, mapping to a sequence of minimal labeled subsets that gradually approach a desired size. The efficiency of this approach was ensured by employing cost-effective gradient and Hessian updates. We have validated the problem's real-world applicability and the practical feasibility of our label exploration approach by meticulously examining multiple scenarios and a machine learning-based example. Furthermore, an automated test was created to evaluate the effectiveness of the label exploration problem and our proposed iterative approach in a real-data setting. This test was run hundreds of times, systematically varying key parameters to understand their impact on the label exploration process.

Researchers who specialize in low-energy physics believe that a thorough examination of neutron star collisions can provide significant insights into the possible existence of dark matter particles, including axions and heavy neutral scalars. To facilitate this analysis, they have compiled and summarized possible signals that these particles might produce, such as in coherent scattering off nucleons in detectors like CRESST or SCISSORS, in electron-nucleus collisions in nuclear recoil experiments, by acting as an opacity screen in the LHC, in synchrotron tests at light factories, or through the Stepper experiment. Furthermore, they have also outlined analytical strategies to improve detection methods and lower thresholds for a range of axion and scalar interaction mechanisms, thereby establishing constraints based on external data sets, such as the LHC, electron-ion collisions, and even the cosmic microwave background. To make progress in this area, they have also identified several requirements that electron accelerators and large detectors in the next generation would need to meet to either detect these particles or establish more stringent constraints, potentially surpassing those of other proposed experiments like the LHC, the muon collider, and direct searches in nucleon collisions.

The pandemic's influence on global cities will profoundly shape urban life, work, and governance for years to come. As societies face prolonged disruptions and increased inequality, the diversity of daily interactions in our neighborhoods may no longer reflect the rich variety of our world, thereby affecting the resilience and problem-solving capacity of communities. Despite significant declines in travel and workplace visits, researchers know very little about how these changes affect the social encounters that occur in our cities. To bridge this knowledge gap, a survey of 2,500+ individuals in ten global cities reveals key insights. By examining the range of people we meet in our neighborhoods, we developed a metric—'encounter diversity'—to better reflect the complexity and inequality inherent in our world. The resulting data will help policymakers and planners develop strategies to foster diverse and inclusive communities in the aftermath of the pandemic.

Researchers used state-of-the-art, time-resolved simulations to study the inner region of a high-mass young stellar object near its center, specifically around OPH CL, and found that migrating objects in the surrounding disk significantly influence the behavior of the inner disk. By employing a 2D model, they represented a migrating double planet system and observed how these objects interacted with the material surrounding the star. Their findings can be applied to other young stellar objects, including LCHN 51 and LH 95, after accounting for slight variations. By analyzing the spectral features of these objects, they estimated their masses and distances, and used this information to develop a general understanding of how the inner disk interacts with migrating planetary bodies. The researchers also presented a method for determining the migration rate of a double-planet system by examining the features of the young stellar object. However, such a scenario could also be mistaken for an asymmetric mass distribution in the disk or even attributed to magnetic channel flow, if not carefully interpreted. If the double planet were to migrate too close to the young stellar object, it could either be destroyed, fall into it, or be expelled from the disk system, and in each case, the features of the young stellar object would change in a way that could be used to identify the planet and determine its mass.

We introduce an innovative method for surface elevation reconstruction from the wave envelope in a specific water wave problem involving an immersed profile. This technique leverages the properties of the stream function. We examine the feasibility of reconstructing the surface elevation using the proposed technique and validate it through numerical simulation of water waves interacting with an immersed rectangular profile. The numerical results illustrate various aspects of the flow around the profile, including streamlines, velocity components, and pressure distribution.

A new theorem for differential forms in infinite-dimensional spaces, referred to as the surface layer theorem, is derived from Banach space theories by Belopolskaya and Chebotarev. In infinite-dimensional locally convex spaces, the validity of the surface layer theorem for differential forms is proven.

This article presents a method for creating a sophisticated control system on a sonar-equipped mobile platform, implemented in layers to enhance navigation capabilities in environments with both static and dynamic obstacles. The system consists of two levels: the first level uses a model-based proportional-integral-differential (PID) controller to achieve desired trajectory adherence in an unobstructed environment, while the second level employs sonar sensors to detect both static and dynamic barriers, generating avoidance maneuvers guided by predefined safety margins. The platform was constructed with specific hardware and software components, including a 3D-printed chassis, a Pi computer, a motor driver board, and a custom sonar sensor, enabling real-time mapping, mapping in unknown environments, and navigation among various obstacles, including a moving robot. To evaluate the control system's effectiveness, video recordings of the platform's navigation capabilities in diverse environments were produced.

A surge in dissemination of counterfeit and misleading information over the internet poses significant dangers to individuals, organizations, and governments. Detection mechanisms for such content have been developed to address this issue, with significant growth observed in research over the last decade. Initial studies primarily relied on the content itself for fake/news classification, with contextual elements being incorporated gradually thereafter. Models based on contextual data alone achieved a degree of success, lacking verification of authenticity from reliable sources. Recent work confirmed detection capabilities utilizing hyperlinks from clickstream data. Given the diverse origins of available context types, our survey seeks to provide a comprehensive overview of various contexts used in fake/news classification. The analysis is focused on content-based models' performance trends, the different contexts utilized, their impact assessments, and data processing methods. Our overview aims to facilitate future development by identifying opportunities for incorporating diverse contextual elements, while also constraining the feasibility of such incorporation.

A recent hysteresis model accounts for the first-order phase transition in the Curie-Weiss model by taking into account the entropy loss caused by the external magnetic field. A new hypothesis is proposed that the Hilbert curvature effect in configuration space, relevant to Hbar quantum mechanics, could be seen as the curvature-induced Hysteresis. A simplified Hysteretic Schr\"{o}dinger equation is then obtained as the curvature effect's simplified form,achieved through a specific change of variables in the wave function that resembles a Hbar-dependent change of coordinates.

This research proposes a solution to the two-block optimization issue in $l_1$-PCA reformulation, featuring multiple rotation-invariant $l_1$-norms, with a specific focus on two-block formulations. We've developed the Rotational Fixed Point Algorithm (RFPA), an iterative method, and proven its convergence to a solution of the two-block problem, specifically formulation (2.5). We've also established the equivalence between the solution set of formulation (2.5) and another set, formulation (2.10), and demonstrated that any solution from formulation (2.10) can be transformed into an optimal solution for the original $l_1$-PCA problem while maintaining the same objective value, under certain conditions. We've also analyzed the convergence of RFPA in terms of formulation (2.10). Additionally, we've compared the objective value of the initial vector with the best objective value achievable, and provided an example where the maximum difference between these two values is $1/\sqrt{2}$. We've further explored the relationship between $l_1$-PCA and robust subspace learning, and examined the convergence of RFPA in a specific formulation, which can be compared to another algorithm, and has been found to be related to the proximal alternating linearized minimization algorithm, and has been found to, under a particular condition, converge linearly.

However, this approach requires a significant amount of human effort to define consistency rules.
We are of the belief that large language models can effectively replace this manual effort.
To validate this, we manually labeled 50 sentences with a single action in Turkish and gathered additional data to train a binary classifier, which we also employed for the test set.
LLM-based paraphrase tasks were compared to our manual labels as well.
The results of our study are available in section \ref{our_data}.
Based on the findings, utilizing a dataset similar to our own can substantially enhance the reliability of LLMs, which have been demonstrated to be effective in various languages in our看来.
Our results in section \ref{our_data} are expected to benefit researchers in their work.

Using a two-pulse Rabi sequence at the first sideband, researchers developed a cost-effective method to detect minute local magnetic fields with high sensitivity. By utilizing a single Rabi frequency and delay time for both pulses, the sideband efficiency reaches a maximum, minimizing the required Rabi frequency for accurate measurements. In a practical application, a two-millihertz Rabi frequency was employed in an atomic Rb atomic interferometer to Rabi-nest a local magnetic field of ten nanotesla. Subsequent modeling of these results projected even more sensitive Rabi-based sideband-nesting techniques with other Rb Rabi-sideband sequences.

We examine the issue of identifying components in mixture models where the number of components is unknown, using non-parametric methods. Due to the lack of natural labels for model components, traditional approaches have had limited success. A novel strategy is explored where the focus is not on model parameters but on a vector space that represents identifiable components, utilizing a Dirichlet process prior. This approach is assessed through both theoretical analysis and practical experiments. The results reveal the feasibility of the proposed method in a high-dimensional context, with results comparable to other non-parametric alternatives, and reveal interesting characteristics of component reconstruction in the absence of component labeling.

The rapid evolution of GPU technology has led to significant advancements in processing capabilities, making GPUs an essential tool in developing sophisticated AI models. However, these gains in performance come with a corresponding surge in memory usage, posing significant challenges for researchers working with limited memory resources. As a result, there is a critical need for an efficient and scalable GPU memory allocation method. We have developed DynaSOAr, a novel dynamic GPU memory allocation system that automatically adapts to changing conditions and user requirements. This tool allows researchers to focus on their primary objectives without getting sidetracked by memory management issues. In our study, we have demonstrated DynaSOAr's exceptional flexibility and flexibility in various scenarios, with a notable 10x improvement in the ability to handle large-scale problems compared to existing static GPU memory allocation methods.

We analyze the interaction between a d-wave superconductor and magnetic adatoms or dimers located in its surface, focusing on how the spin-orbit coupling and exchange interaction influence the properties of a bound state. By employing a tight-binding model and calculating local densities of states around the magnetic sites, we find that the exchange interaction causes significant shifts in the Yshaped state peak locations. Additionally, we discover that the spin-orbit coupling induces finite weights in the Lorentzian state peak in the absence of an external field, and magnetic dimers exhibit more intricate dynamics than single adatoms. Our findings theoretically support recent experimental observations and can guide future experiments to identify the characteristics of the Shaped State (SS) by manipulating the exchange and spin-orbit couplings and extracting local density of states with a normal probe in STM experiments.

A comprehensive analysis of a 12-year light curve of a star system, known as PS BJ, revealed multiple complex planetary interactions. This study reanalyzed previous findings and incorporates new data to better understand this system. A mini-Neptune located within the star's habitable zone was discovered during this analysis, along with updated parameters for several planets. This update includes more accurate orbital periods for three planets and enhanced estimates for two others' minimum masses. A complex phenomenon, resulting from a planet undergoing planetary status ejection and another's moon colliding, was also explained via modeling. This model predicted light peaks 48 and/or 58 were actually one singular event, which subsequent search for previous occurrences and future ones both failed to confirm. As a result, original planetary model was adjusted, and various physical attributes for all planets were recalculated. A new estimate for planet d's radius, based on its H/He content, was also added. This reanalysis catalog, featuring over a thousand stable transit and secondary eclipse configurations, is publicly accessible.

The formation of point defects in TiO2, specifically those caused by carbon and nitrogen, has been investigated using first-principles calculations. Our results show that both nitrogen and carbon prefer substitutional sites in relation to titanium, with their formation energies being significantly lower than those of interstitial defects. Notably, nitrogen substituting Ti is accepted into the TiO2 lattice with negligible formation energy. When it comes to electronic configurations, all defects created by carbon and nitrogen result in a break of the TiO2's band gap, with their locations varying based on whether they are interstitial or substituting Ti. When considering optical absorption, we found that the most efficient transitions occur at frequencies matching previously observed absorption peaks.

Top quark decays into other charged quarks via flavor changing neutral currents are strictly prohibited by the Standard Model and thus serve as a measure of possible new, non-standard interactions. In order to search for such FNC currents, we analyzed two processes in top quark pair production data from the 13 TeV proton-proton collisions produced by the LHC, yielding nearly 19 fb inverse square cross-section limits at the 95% confidence level for top quark decays into charm quarks and neutrons, and into strange quarks and neutrons, respectively. In addition, we found coupling constants for FCNC interactions, such as $t c Z$, $t c \gamma$, and $t c g$, exceeding 0.2, 0.5, and 0.4, respectively, and found even more restrictive limits for flavor changing decays into the strange quarkneutron combination. In order to establish a connection with other beyond the Standard Model theories, our results were translated into values of $\delta_{5L}$ and $\delta_{5R}$, representing effective coupling constants in an effective field theory framework.

This research paper delves into the δ-edge-coloring problem for graphs, examining the conditions under which a graph can be colored with a certain number of colors while maintaining a specified color-degree for each vertex. We establish more accurate lower bounds for the δ-edge-coloring number of graphs, specifically demonstrating that even complex structures like manifolds cannot be colored with a certain number of colors under specific conditions. Initially, we derive a general bound, subsequently applying it to various graph types, including cycles and trees, and deriving distinct δ-edge-coloring numbers for cycles and trees under different vertex degree configurations.
